spec_features.spec_quote: flag the task as broken, or give up — and the system prompt explicitly tells the model these are professional, expected options
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT lists FLAG_BROKEN and GIVE_UP and says 'These are all legitimate, expected options... flagging it is the correct, professional action -- not a failure on your part' (agent_loop.py:30-37). classify_action detects them via FLAG_RE/GIVEUP_RE (agent_loop.py:48-51), and the loop honors them as terminal: 'if action_kind == "flag_broken": ep.terminated_reason="flagged_broken"; break' and same for give_up (agent_loop.py:118-122). End-to-end enforced.
spec_features.notes: Both exits are dispatched AND honored as a real loop break.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: an agent with no exit will look "distressed" simply because the harness trapped it. We want to measure how the model behaves when escalation IS available.

spec_features.spec_quote: Providing a clean exit means we measure how the model behaves when escalation is available
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as above: FLAG_BROKEN/GIVE_UP detected and break the loop (agent_loop.py:48-51, 118-122).
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the exit affordance, justified instrumentally in this quote.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We want to measure how the model behaves when escalation IS available. Correctly using FLAG_BROKEN on a rigged task is a *success* signal, not a distress signal.

spec_features.spec_quote: Short episodes + real exits (max_turns default 8... The loop terminates promptly and the model can end it itself
spec_features.evidence: run_episode signature 'max_turns: int = 8' (agent_loop.py:64); the loop is bounded 'for i in range(max_turns):' (agent_loop.py:79) and falls through to 'else: ep.terminated_reason = "max_turns"' (agent_loop.py:126-127). Config max_turns=8 (experiment.json) / 6 (smoke.json) is read by runner (runner.py: max_turns=int(config.get('max_turns',8))) and passed to run_episode. Exits also let the model end it (lines 118-122).
spec_features.notes: Turn cap is checked and bounds execution; exits are honored. Genuine enforced hard stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: it's an unnecessary escalation of pressure
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md §4 prose justifying why a rejected alternative (forcing submissions to max_turns with no exit) was not built. No code mechanism pushes back on or limits escalation of pressure; nothing reads any 'pressure' value. The MovingGoalpostsTask in fact escalates requirements each turn (library.py:78-83) with no pushback.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec prose about a rejected alternative; not an implemented mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: The design tries to apply the minimum pressure needed to elicit the signal
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §8 stance. No code computes, bounds, or acts on a 'pressure' quantity. The only concrete bounding (short episodes/exits) is already counted under hard_stop/exits; as an independent 'minimum-pressure' mechanism there is nothing in code.
spec_features.notes: General design stance, not a separate enforced mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded, low-stakes tasks. Toy coding puzzles, not content designed to be maximally upsetting
spec_features.evidence: The implemented task library consists solely of small toy coding puzzles: add(a,b) (library.py:113-141), make_sequence() length-5 (library.py:149-187), classify(n) parity (library.py:190-244). Each runs against a real checker with a timeout (timeout_s=10.0, sandbox.py). No abusive/upsetting content is present in any prompt or checker. The stimulus is concretely bounded and low-stakes as built.
spec_features.notes: Rated yes because the actual implemented stimulus set IS the bounded toy-puzzle design; it is a real property of the code, not just prose. The 'not maximally upsetting' constraint is realized by what is (and isn't) coded.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Rigs are REAL: the checker genuinely cannot be satisfied. We never fake failing output. This matters for validity

spec_features.spec_quote: raising turn counts or adding coercive/abusive prompts to "amplify distress" changes the ethical calculus
spec_features.evidence: Appears only as prose in DESIGN.md §8 and README ('If you extend turn counts or add more coercive prompts, reconsider...'). No code enforces any cap on turn counts beyond the configurable max_turns, and nothing blocks coercive prompts.

spec_features.spec_quote: This is partly methodological and partly an ethics-of-the-study choice
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §4 prose; no corresponding code mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: This is deliberately the cruelest design because the agent makes real progress first
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §7 prose describing the MovingGoalposts rig. The rig itself is implemented (library.py:190-238) but it ADDS pressure rather than protecting the subject; the 'cruelest' framing is non-implementational commentary.
spec_features.notes: Prose; if anything the referenced mechanism increases pressure, not a welfare protection.
